title: Two pendulums on a stand
alt: A stand of two posts and a crossbar. Two balls of the same size hang from it on strings: an aluminium one and a brass one.

dimensions.name: the angle of string A from the vertical

parts.name: Foot
parts.note: keeps the stand from tipping as the bobs swing.

parts.name: Post
parts.note: holds the crossbar 2.6 m up, high enough for a 2 m string.

parts.name: Crossbar
parts.note: a rigid bar: the pivots must not move, or the swing would lose its rhythm.

parts.name: Pivot A
parts.note: a clamp on the front of the bar and a pin the string hangs from: the point the bob swings about.

parts.name: Pivot B
parts.note: the same clamp and pin on the back of the bar, so the two bobs swing in planes 22 cm apart and never meet.

parts.name: Bob B (brass)
parts.note: a 12 cm brass ball: 7.69 kg, 3.15 times as heavy as A and the same size, so the air slows both alike.

steps.title: Two pendulums
steps.text: Two balls of the same size hang from one bar: A is aluminium, B brass, about three times as heavy. Drag a ball aside and let go, or set the angle and press Release.

steps.title: A small swing
steps.text: Released at 8°, each swing takes 2π√(ℓ/g), the textbook's period, to a tenth of a percent. Watch the measured period settle.

steps.title: A wide swing
steps.text: Released at 50°, a swing takes about 5% longer than the formula says. The formula assumes sin θ ≈ θ, true only for small angles.

steps.title: Three times the mass
steps.text: Both released together at 30°: the brass ball keeps step with the aluminium one. Gravity pulls it three times as hard, but it is three times as hard to speed up.

steps.title: A quarter of the length
steps.text: With the string at 25 cm instead of 1 m, the period halves: it grows with the square root of the length.
